Your Father's Open Care Issues on One Page

Who holds each one, who to contact, and which ones have no one yet.

Download PDF

The notes from the last family call are in three different phones, and nobody is sure who said they'd call the doctor's office.

This page doesn't ask you to solve any of it. It asks what is open, where the notes about it are, who is holding it, and who there is to contact.

The open issues

One line for each issue, in a few plain words. If nobody is holding it, leave that box empty.

What has no one yet

Every open issue with an empty “who is holding it” box, and anything in the second list that nobody can find. Put a name beside each one only when that person has said yes.

For example Rescheduling the appointment: nobody has said they'll call. My brother has the notes from Sunday but hasn't sent them around.

How to use it

  • Don't retell an issue or explain it here. Name it, and say where the notes are.
  • An empty box shows where a gap is. It isn't a comment on anyone.
  • Write the date beside each note. If a note has no date, write “undated.”
  • Keep the page where everyone in the family can see it, and bring it to the next call.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't say what any note, record or instruction means, which issue matters most, or who should have been holding it. It shows where things are and where nobody is yet.

Where this comes from

Keeping shared notes where everyone involved can reach them follows the National Institute on Aging's advice on sharing caregiving responsibilities. The rows come from the Family Care Roadmap's working list for this step.
